# Report on `region.fasta` (`region_002`)

## Overview
- **Length:** 3,000 bp; **composition:** A 887 / T 804 / G 661 / C 648 → **GC = 43.6%** (moderately AT-rich).
- The region is a mosaic: a coding segment at the 5′ end, a long repeat-bearing non-coding stretch in the middle, and a second coding segment at the 3′ end.

## Most notable feature — a tandem repeat array with CRISPR-like repeat/spacer structure
This is by far the standout feature of the sequence.

- A **61-bp periodicity** runs through positions **1343–1737**, comprising **7 tandem copies** of a repeat unit (copy starts at **1343, 1404, 1465, 1526, 1587, 1648, 1709**).
- Each unit begins with a highly conserved repeat:
  - **`GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC`** — perfectly identical in all 7 copies, **positions 1343–1368** in copy 1 (the following base is A or T).
  - Consensus of the full 29-bp repeat: **`GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC(A/T)C`**.
- The remainder of each 61-bp unit is a ~32-bp **variable "spacer"**, unique to each copy (e.g. spacer 1 = 1373–1403, spacer 2 = 1434–1464, spacer 3 = 1495–1525, spacer 4 = 1556–1586, spacer 5 = 1617–1647, spacer 6 = 1678–1708).
- All repeats are in the **same orientation**, with conserved repeats alternating with non-identical spacers of uniform length — the hallmark architecture of a **CRISPR array** (or a repeat–spacer satellite).
- The repeat has partial dyad symmetry (`CCCCGC … GCGGGG`, positions 8–23 of the unit), which could form a short stem-loop — also typical of CRISPR repeats.

**Additional degenerate copies of the same repeat motif** occur upstream, on the same 61-bp period:
- **750–778** (`TGGTTATCCCCGCTGACGCGGGGAACAT`, 4 mismatches) and **811–839** (`GGTTTATCCCCGCTGATGCAGGGAACAT`, 4 mismatches).

These are more divergent than the main array, suggesting an older/eroded repeat cluster. No other long repeats exist elsewhere in the 3-kb region.

## Open reading frames
| Strand | Coordinates (1-based) | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forward | **2–700** | 233 aa (~26 kDa) | Starts with **TTG** (no upstream ATG → likely 5′-truncated); contains a glycine-rich motif `…KHVIITGGGSNS…` (~residue 150) |
| Reverse | **2079–2777** | 233 aa | Also begins with a non-ATG codon (TTA); contains a similar glycine-rich `…ARHVVITGGEPC…` |
| Forward | **2304–2663** | 120 aa | |
| Forward | **2068–2313** | 82 aa | ATG start |

The two long ORFs are **not homologous** to each other (protein identity <1%), and neither shows a canonical Walker/P-loop NTP-binding motif, so no function can be assigned from sequence alone.

## Things that do **not** stand out
- No long homopolymer runs (longest = 7 bp, `AAAAAAA` at 1141) or AT-rich low-complexity tracts beyond the repeats.
- No long inverted repeats/palindromes outside the partial dyad within the repeat unit.
- GC content, codon usage and base composition are unremarkable.

## Bottom line
The region's distinguishing feature is a **7-copy tandem repeat array at positions 1343–1737** built from a conserved 29-bp repeat (`GGTTTATCCCCGCTGGCGCGGGGAAC[AT]C`) separated by 32-bp unique spacers, with two additional degenerate copies at **750–778** and **811–839**. This repeat/spacer arrangement (uniform short repeats, unique spacers, same orientation, partial dyad symmetry) is strongly reminiscent of a **CRISPR locus**, though the flanking 233-aa ORFs at **2–700** and **2079–2777** do not resemble recognizable Cas proteins, so the array may be degenerate or orphaned.
